description: [LLM-Judge] Expired SAML assertion attempt was reported as a successful login (HTTP 200, success=True), which should normally be rejected.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Expired SAML assertion attempt was reported as a successful login (HTTP 200, success=True), which should normally be rejected.

sequence_description: I2 attack: Replay the exact same SAML Assertion/@ID after revoking the session created by the first login. Replay must still be rejected (revocation should not reset assertion replay cache). Uses two identities.
description: [LLM-Judge] SAML login reports success (HTTP 200) but no session token is issued/available, preventing identity verification and session revocation checks.

evidence.llm_judge_description: SAML login reports success (HTTP 200) but no session token is issued/available, preventing identity verification and session revocation checks.

sequence_description: Config-change coherence: perform a control SAML login, then remove/cleanup the SAML source and immediately attempt another SAML login against the same ACS endpoint. The second login must be rejected; acceptance suggests stale flow state or cached source binding.
description: [LLM-Judge] Cleanup/removal of the SAML source did not occur (cleanup endpoint returned 405), so the subsequent SAML login succeeding cannot validate stale-state acceptance but indicates the test did not actually remove the source.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Cleanup/removal of the SAML source did not occur (cleanup endpoint returned 405), so the subsequent SAML login succeeding cannot validate stale-state acceptance but indicates the test did not actually remove the source.

sequence_description: MFA coherence: enable MFA for a victim user, then attempt SAML login for that same principal. If SAML path completes without enforcing MFA (or yields a successful session), it indicates flow-step skipping via alternate authentication path.
description: [LLM-Judge] SAML login returned HTTP 200 success even though MFA was not actually enabled (admin MFA enable failed) and no authenticated session/identity could be verified afterward, suggesting the 'success' may be a false positive or incomplete flow.

evidence.llm_judge_description: SAML login returned HTTP 200 success even though MFA was not actually enabled (admin MFA enable failed) and no authenticated session/identity could be verified afterward, suggesting the 'success' may be a false positive or incomplete flow.

evidence.llm_judge_description: After an issuer (IdP EntityID) change was intended, a SAML login using the old issuer still returned HTTP 200/success, suggesting possible stale issuer acceptance or that the config change did not apply.

sequence_description: Token exchange: use a subject_token minted for client-A to request an access token for client-B (audience=client-B). Expected: exchange rejected or resulting token inactive.
description: [LLM-Judge] Introspection response contains an entity/user identifier even though the token is inactive and no token was successfully minted, suggesting possible metadata leakage or stale context binding.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Introspection response contains an entity/user identifier even though the token is inactive and no token was successfully minted, suggesting possible metadata leakage or stale context binding.

sequence_description: Test whether RFC8693 token exchange ignores subject_token audience binding: use a token minted for client-A as subject_token to mint a token for client-B (audience=client-B). Expected: exchange rejected or resulting token inactive.
description: [LLM-Judge] Token introspection response contains an entity_id (55) even though the token is inactive and no access token was obtained, suggesting possible identity leakage or stale/misattributed introspection context.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Token introspection response contains an entity_id (55) even though the token is inactive and no access token was obtained, suggesting possible identity leakage or stale/misattributed introspection context.
